notes.title: Tezcatlipoca V 1.035 – Speedrun Contest
notes.content:
[h2]🏆 [b]Tezcatlipoca V 1.035 – Speedrun Contest[/b][/h2][p]
Hello, dear players! With this update comes a very important change: [b]Tezcatlipoca now has a timer![/b] And with it… the [b]first official Tezcatlipoca Speedrun Contest[/b] is now open![/p][p][/p][h2]What is the contest about?[/h2][p]The goal is simple:[/p][list][*][p][b]Get ending E on the hardest difficulty in the shortest possible time.[/b][/p][/*][*][p]Deaths [b]don’t matter[/b], so you can die as many times as you want.[/p][/*][/list][h2]How to participate?[/h2][olist][*][p]Record your run in [b]one single video[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]The video must start from a [b]new game[/b] and end when you reach the final scene of the game.[/p][/*][*][p]Upload your video to [b]YouTube[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Share the link on the [b]official Tezcatlipoca forums[/b].[/p][/*][/olist][p][b]Deadline:[/b] October 31, 2025 🎃 Happy Halloween![/p][p][/p][h1]Prizes[/h1][p]The [b]top 3 players[/b] will be immortalized in the game:[/p][list][*][p]Their names will appear in the official achievements with [b]gold, silver, and bronze medals[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Each winner will also receive [b]an extra copy of Tezcatlipoca[/b] to gift to a friend.[/p][/*][/list][p]There will also be [b]special categories for endings A, B, C, and D[/b], on any difficulty:[/p][list][*][p]Each ending will have a [b]Top 3[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Winners of each category will also have their names written on the corresponding achievement.[/p][/*][/list][h2]How does the timer work?[/h2][p]The timer is integrated into [b]Minerva[/b].[/p][list][*][p]The time runs in [b]any scene where the player has control[/b].[/p][/*][/list][p]This includes:[/p][list][*][p]Normal gameplay[/p][/*][*][p]Puzzles[/p][/*][*][p]Save screens[/p][/*][/list][p]The time does [b]not run[/b] during:[/p][list][*][p]Flashbacks[/p][/*][*][p]Monster stories[/p][/*][*][p]Pause menu ([b]only exception[/b])[/p][/*][/list][p]⚠️ If you notice the timer not running in a puzzle or situation where it should, please report it.[/p][hr][/hr][h2][b]Results Page – Speedrun[/b][/h2][p]We now have a [b]Results Page[/b] that tracks all the key information from your run![/p][p][b]What it shows:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Total speedrun time[/p][/*][*][p]Number of deaths[/p][/*][*][p]Saves performed[/p][/*][*][p]Difficulty chosen[/p][/*][*][p]Ending obtained[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Coming soon:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Official [b]rankings[/b] after the speedrun contest ends[/p][/*][*][p]Adjusted times to make them [b]achievable for average players[/b][/p][/*][/list][p]Get ready to [b]track your progress and compare yourself with the best![/b][/p][hr][/hr][h2][b]New Puzzle – Residential Area[/b][/h2][p]A [b]new puzzle[/b] has been added to access the residential area.
If you are playing with an older save and decide to leave this area, you will need to [b]solve the puzzle to re-enter[/b].[/p][p][b]How the puzzle works:[/b][/p][list][*][p]The goal is to obtain a [b]resident ID[/b] by entering information about the inhabitants.[/p][/*][*][p]There are [b]two possible solutions[/b] in my design, but if the puzzle feels too confusing, don’t hesitate to let me know![/p][/*][/list][p][b]Changes to the entrance of the residential area:[/b][/p][list][*][p]The entrance now has a [b]physical door[/b]. No more crawling to get through![/p][/*][*][p]This change [b]alters the flow of the game[/b], forcing the player to visit the [b]cemetery first[/b] before continuing the story.[/p][/*][/list][p][b]Why this change?[/b][/p][list][*][p]I liked leaving the city open for free exploration, but I realized:[/p][list][*][p]Without a clear direction, the experience could feel [b]boring or confusing[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]Arriving at the residential area and not finding Becky until later could be tedious.[/p][/*][/list][/*][*][p]Blocking this area and requiring the puzzle ensures that the player explores the other zone first, [b]making the direction clearer[/b] and improving story progression.[/p][/*][/list]

notes.title: Actualización V 1.031
notes.content:
[h1]Update V 1.031[/h1][p]Hello dear players!
The quality-of-life improvements for [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] never stop—this time, we’re giving a little more weight to the [b]school[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][h2]Why the school?[/h2][p]The initial concept of [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] took place entirely within a school, inspired by a kindergarten near my house. While walking my dogs at night, I noticed one of the school’s lights flickering, and it struck me as incredibly eerie.[/p][hr][/hr][h2]Changes inside the school[/h2][list][*][p] The [b]nahual[/b] can now appear inside the small mazes.[/p][/*][*][p]Access to the [b]basketball court maze[/b] now requires the broken dagger.[/p][/*][*][p]A new sound has been added to guide players into investigating the men’s bathroom, once Mary has been freed.[/p][/*][*][p]A new [b]3D model[/b] has been added at the school entrance to indicate when the padlock is still locked.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]Notable changes[/h2][list][*][p]Player [b]walking and running speed[/b] in the “danger state” has been increased.
Even though enemies aren’t an immediate threat, moving slowly while injured could feel frustrating—even for me as the developer. I increased the speed slightly, without matching the healthy state, to keep the discomfort but still prioritize survival.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]The park is no longer safe![/h2][p]Although I wanted this to remain a surprise, I have to share it here for transparency:[/p][list][*][p]The [b]park is no longer a safe zone[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]A new [b]random scare[/b] may appear.[/p][/*][*][p]After obtaining either the [b]Immaculate Heart[/b] or the [b]Corrupted Heart[/b], some extra decorations will show up.[/p][/*][/list][p]This is part of a larger plan to add more small surprises and details to different areas of the game. Stay tuned to see what else I’m cooking up![/p][hr][/hr][h2]Pharmacy update[/h2][p]The pharmacy received a small update—just a little creepier now. There’s also a minor scare, but this new room may be linked to future updates. [/p][hr][/hr][h2]Becky’s house[/h2][list][*][p]Becky’s house is now [b]locked[/b] until you unlock the park gate.[/p][/*][*][p]This change is meant to guide players: once you reach the end of the residential area, you’ll know that Becky lives there and understand that you should return later.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]Future plans[/h2][list][*][p]Expanding the [b]church[/b], possibly adding an underground level.[/p][/*][*][p]Continuing to refine level design while sticking to the [b]low-poly rule[/b].[/p][/*][*][p]More environmental scares and details coming in future updates.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h2]Thank you[/h2][p]Thank you for playing, supporting, and sending feedback. Every comment helps [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] grow![/p]

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca – More on Development & Version 1.03
notes.content:
[h1]Tezcatlipoca – More on Development & Version 1.03[/h1][p]Hello, dear players.[/p][p]I’d like to share with you the most important changes in this new version, along with some reflections on the future of the game.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Main Changes[/h3][p][b]– Mandatory Mary Summoning[/b]
Starting with this version, summoning Mary’s spirit is now required in order to leave the school.[/p][p][b]Why this change?[/b]
Some players were able to progress through a large portion of the game without summoning her, which made the experience less engaging—especially in the early hours, where only the “Skullies” appeared.[/p][p]To maintain tension and increase the challenge from the very beginning, summoning Mary in the school is now mandatory.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]– New NPC: Mister Iniestra[/b]
Mister Iniestra has hidden himself inside the school. If you’re playing on an advanced save file and return to this area, you’ll need to find him—alive or dead—in order to leave. Otherwise, you’ll be trapped![/p][p](Please report any issues with backwards compatibility; every time I add something, there’s a risk of breaking something else 😅).[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Gameplay Adjustments[/h3][list][*][p]Reduced the stun duration when being hit or surprised by small enemies.[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed a collision in Becky’s house that allowed players to clip through walls.[/p][/*][*][p]Expanded the crouch/uncrouch collision areas to avoid serious bugs on systems running the game at low FPS.[/p][/*][*][p]Added 3 new random “scares” in certain areas (mostly sound-based). More will be added in future versions.[/p][/*][/list][hr][/hr][h3]The Future of Tezcatlipoca[/h3][p]I’m still polishing details of the game. I’ve been going through some difficult emotional and mental moments, but that doesn’t mean the project is abandoned.[/p][p]My intention is to keep adding content that makes the first half of the game scarier and more engaging.[/p][p]In that sense, integrating Mary as an enemy so early on feels like a big step in maintaining constant tension. It might not be obvious at first glance, but Mary is actually my favorite specter in the game.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]Inspirations Behind Tezcatlipoca[/h3][p]The main inspiration for the story was, without a doubt, [b]Silent Hill 1[/b]. I always felt it told a simpler, more grounded story in a godforsaken town—just like Tezcatlipoca. A sect that performs sacrifices to summon their god… that became the foundation.[/p][p]Mixing that concept with a small town in Mexico made the outcome feel very natural. Aware of my limits as a writer, I also leaned toward the tone of the early [b]Resident Evil[/b] games: less seriousness and more of a B-movie vibe. Even the crushing doors that open and close on the player are a little reference to the famous “Jill Sandwich” line… or in this case, a “Minerva Sandwich.”[/p][p]Sadly, I never played [b]Alone in the Dark[/b], which might be the game most visually similar to mine, but the idea of making Tezcatlipoca low poly came from [b]Ashen[/b], a gorgeous soulslike built entirely in that style.[/p][p]The storytelling and NPC interactions were inspired by [b]Dark Souls[/b]. For me, it’s the simplest way to handle characters without the need for elaborate cutscenes or complex animations during dialogue.[/p][p]As for literary influences, the clearest one is [b]Lovecraft[/b]. I’m a big fan of [i]The Call of Cthulhu[/i], though personally I prefer stories like [i]The Outsider[/i]. Cosmic horror has always fascinated me, though I’ll admit I’m not a big reader in general.[/p][p]And of course, the biggest gameplay influence is [b]Haunting Ground[/b]: a game where combat barely exists, but you explore a hauntingly beautiful castle full of memorable enemies and atmosphere.[/p][p]I still have a long way to go in terms of level design, but in the future I’d love to create something closer to the classic [b]Resident Evil[/b] style, especially that intense combat I loved so much in [i]Resident Evil 3: Nemesis[/i].[/p][hr][/hr][p]I hope you enjoy this new version, and as always, thank you so much for all your support.[/p][p]And well… I hope you have a great time playing [i]Hollow Knight: Silksong[/i], which  is a much better game than mine! 😆[/p]

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca V 1.03
notes.content:
[p]Hello, dear players.
This update is small, but by no means less important![/p][p][b]Highlighted Changes[/b][/p][p][b]Space Valkyries:[/b][/p][list][*][p]Now features the amazing music of the talented Nobu Mortem.[/p][/*][*][p]A special shot has been added, which you can activate using the Run button.[/p][/*][*][p]We’ve introduced indestructible asteroids that orbit the stage and destroy the player on contact. Watch out![/p][/*][/list][p][b]Reverse Movement:[/b] It’s now possible to walk backwards while crouching, making it easier to solve the game’s very first puzzle.[/p][p][b]Future Plans[/b][/p][p]A brand-new minigame is planned. However, I’m currently going through a bit of creative block, which has delayed its development. Still, it remains firmly in the plans.[/p][p]I’m also exploring ideas for a [b]New Game+ mode[/b], though I’m not yet certain what kind of benefits would make sense to add, considering that [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] doesn’t feature ammo or permanent upgrades (beyond the health increase from finding hearts).[/p][p]One of the most tempting proposals is to add an [b]invulnerability mode[/b] as a special reward for those who complete the game on the hardest difficulty.[/p][p]Thank you so much for continuing to follow the development and for all your support![/p]

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca – Level and Puzzle Design
notes.content:
[p]In [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i], there are two main types of puzzles: logical and mechanical.[/p][p]🔹 [b]Logical Puzzles[/b]
These are like the USB one, where you need to switch all the squares to “0.” They are based on reading and understanding the clues you find throughout the game. I believe the hints I provide are enough, but if any puzzle ends up being too complicated, your feedback is always welcome![/p][p]🔹 [b]Mechanical Puzzles[/b]
These include sections with moving platforms, areas where you need to crouch, or avoid falling. The intention is for the player to interact more directly with the environment.[/p][p]However, what I’m most proud of are the enemies: each one is, in itself, a small puzzle.[/p][list][*][p]Some are repelled by light.[/p][/*][*][p]Others only damage the player if they remain standing.[/p][/*][*][p]Others are triggered only if you run or walk close to them.[/p][/*][/list][p]This means that encountering enemies —and combinations of them— becomes a dynamic puzzle the player must solve on the spot, making the right decision in order to survive.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Level Design[/b][/p][p]My levels often take the shape of a cross, a design I feel naturally drawn to. The town of [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] was created to feel overwhelming at first, but quickly familiar and recognizable, even without the need for an on-screen map.[/p][p]During development, I considered making the buildings grow darker as the game progressed, but with the low-poly style I felt it would lose impact. Instead, I decided that when players revisit already explored areas, they would find new enemies unlocked, keeping the experience fresh.[/p][p]I also added some “scares” or unsettling moments, but not all of them trigger in every playthrough. The idea is for each player’s experience to feel different, without relying on gratuitous violence or exaggerated effects, but rather maintaining a discreet yet disturbing atmosphere.[/p][hr][/hr][p][b]Why isn’t there a map in the game?[/b][/p][p]Simply put, I couldn’t find a good way to implement it without overwhelming the player. There is a map in the city park that shows the general layout, but since many streets are blocked, I preferred to let the player navigate naturally and memorize the environments.[/p][hr][/hr][p]Reviews are incredibly valuable, as they help [b]Tezcatlipoca[/b] reach a wider audience.[/p][p]If it’s not too much trouble, I’d really appreciate it if you could leave a review —good or bad— as long as it’s honest.[/p][p]And if you’d like, feel free to suggest improvements for the future. Every bit of feedback matters![/p][hr][/hr][p]In the future, I’ll be sharing more about my creative decisions and how [i]Tezcatlipoca[/i] came to be.[/p][p]Is there anything in particular you’d like to know?[/p]

notes.title: About Tezcatlipoca – Creative Process
notes.content:
[p]Hello, dear players.
For those who might be curious, I’d like to share a bit about how [b]Tezcatlipoca[/b] came to life and the process behind its development.[/p][p]From the very beginning, I had a clear idea: I wanted to create a [b]horror game set in contemporary Mexico[/b]. I didn’t have the characters or story defined at first — and maybe that’s why the narrative feels a bit weak, since it was honestly the last thing I worked on. What I really wanted was a game with [b]tank controls, puzzles, and an oppressive atmosphere[/b].[/p][p]At one point, I considered adding combat, but soon realized my current knowledge wouldn’t allow me to properly implement weapons, ammunition, and enemies that stayed dead after being defeated. So I made a key decision: [b]there would be no direct combat[/b]. Similar to [i]Haunting Ground[/i] (a game I really like), I wanted to rely more on atmosphere. That game features stealth mechanics, but I didn’t feel capable of designing scenarios complex enough to make full use of them.[/p][p]Instead, I created a single main enemy: [b]the Llorona/Screamer[/b], an entity that reacts to the sound of the player’s footsteps. That way I could still maintain a stealth element, even if it was only focused on one enemy.[/p][p]I also knew I wanted [b]two first-person scenarios[/b], which gave birth to the labyrinths. The first one, set in a school, was a very simple prototype; later, I expanded on the idea with the labyrinth inside the pyramid.[/p][hr][/hr][h3]The lore of Tezcatlipoca[/h3][p]I always knew the game’s protagonist would be [b]Minerva[/b], a great friend who has always supported my projects. Beyond that, I didn’t really know what direction to take. For a long time, I even toyed with the idea of making the entities extraterrestrial.[/p][p]While looking for fitting names in the Nahuatl language, I remembered one of my earlier projects, [i]Tits and Shadows[/i]. That game had a very small scenario inside a pyramid, with a villain called [b]Tezcatlipoca[/b]. I thought it would be a great idea to expand on that little story and reinterpret it from a new perspective.[/p][p]Human sacrifice and my own culture are deeply connected — almost symbiotically. Once I decided Tezcatlipoca would be the “villain,” everything else became much easier to piece together.[/p][p]The basic story I wrote goes like this:
Minerva arrives in an abandoned town but finds herself unable to leave. The road to another village would take hours, maybe even days on foot, and as we all know, traveling on highways at night is extremely dangerous. So she ventures into the city and begins to see [b]shadows of the past[/b].[/p][p]Most of the inhabitants have disappeared, and some of Minerva’s old acquaintances appear only to show her their mental state crumbling away. In the end, she faces two options: [b]leave the town[/b], or [b]delve deeper into its mysteries and uncover her family’s history[/b].[/p][hr][/hr][p]I know it’s a simple story, but my goal was always to make it effective. Honestly, I’m terrible at writing stories and characters, but I poured a lot of myself into this project. In fact, [b]all of the characters are based on real-life friends[/b], so I also wanted to treat their images with respect inside the game.[/p][p]In short, [b]Tezcatlipoca[/b] was born more out of a desire to create an oppressive atmosphere and gameplay experience than from a carefully crafted narrative. Over time, though, I found the threads that tied the mechanics to the myth — and to my own cultural roots.[/p]

notes.title: Update 1.027
notes.content:
Hello dear players!
In this version we’ve made some small but noticeable adjustments to improve your game experience:

Screamer/Weeping Woman enemy: now has a stun effect radius. If you step out of this range, it will still alert other enemies, but you won’t be stunned anymore!

Particles: some visual effects have been updated. While I’d love to fill the game with flashy and explosive particles, I feel it would hurt the darker and more eerie atmosphere we want to preserve.

Bug Fix: fixed an issue where enemies, when attacking, would cause other enemies to briefly appear and disappear.

Thank you so much for supporting Tezcatlipoca! I hope you enjoy these small changes and what’s yet to come.

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca Soundtrack Now Available
notes.content: [p]Hello dear players,[/p][p]After a long wait, the soundtrack is finally here![/p][p]This means the [i]Tezcatlipoca Collection[/i] can now be purchased with the soundtrack and artbook included, at a [b]20% discount[/b] from the total price.[/p][p]I’m deeply grateful for everyone’s interest, and I hope you enjoy the music from the talented [b]Snap[/b].[/p]

notes.title: Full First-Person Mode & Complete Voice Acting!
notes.content:
[p]Hello dear players,
I’m proud to announce that [b]Neartdubs[/b] has given life to [i]Fabián[/i] with a full professional voice performance. All of his dialogue is now fully voiced![/p][p]I’m also happy to share that the [b]first-person mode[/b] is now fully functional for the entire game. I personally completed a full playthrough in this mode without any issues.[/p][p]
That said, if you happen to encounter any bugs or glitches, please feel free to report them and I’ll fix them as soon as possible.[/p][p][/p][p]Additionally, to complement the new first-person mode, we’ve made some adjustments to the game controls:[/p][list][*][p]To perform a quick 180° turn, you now need to stand still first, then press the run key and the back direction at the same time.[/p][/*][*][p]Pressing only the back direction will make the character walk backwards and exit stealth mode.[/p][/*][/list][p]Please keep this in mind, as it’s [b]crucial[/b] for solving the [b]first puzzle[/b] in the game.[/p][p]
[/p][p][/p][previewyoutube="C90wMFKD-gc;full"][/previewyoutube]

notes.title: Update: First Person Beta + Text Adjustments
notes.content:
We're rolling out a beta version of the First-Person Camera Mode!
Originally not part of the game's design, this new option has been added to the Settings Menu as an experimental feature for players who want to experience the game from a new perspective.

[b]Please note:[/b]

[list]
[*] This is an early implementation, and you may encounter bugs or unexpected behavior.

[*] The final version of the first-person mode is scheduled for release on August 16, including polish and stability fixes.

[*] The game continues to function as intended in third-person mode, but if you notice any issues caused by the new camera option, feel free to report them!
[/list]

[b]Also included in this update:[/b]
[list]
[*] Text size settings for dialogues and many in-game notes. You can now choose between Small, Medium, and Large font sizes.

[*] While most notes have been updated, some may still display formatting issues. Fixes will continue in future patches.
[/list]

Thanks for your support and feedback as we keep improving the game!

notes.title: Text size changes!
notes.content:
I hadn’t considered that some of you might be playing on smaller screens, like the Steam Deck or other handheld devices! The original text size was designed with desktop displays in mind.

As a quickfix, all dialogue text now offers three font size options:
Small, Medium, and Large!

⚠️ This fix does not yet apply to:

[list]
[*] Notes scattered around the world

[*] The Gallery

[*] Books in the Library
[/list]

However, this hotfix lays the groundwork to adjust those fonts in the future! I’ll keep working on expanding this update to cover all text across the game.

For now, I hope this makes reading dialogues much more comfortable!

notes.title: Small Post-Launch Update
notes.content:
This small update focuses on improving the first-person camera, getting ready for a full first-person playthrough of the game!
What's new?

Full compatibility with the mouse to rotate the character and look up/down.

The right stick on gamepads now works just like the mouse for camera control.

Get ready to experience the game from a whole new perspective!

notes.title: Surprise release! Tezcatlipoca has arrived...
notes.content:
[p][b]Surprise release! Tezcatlipoca has arrived...[/b]
A horror game inspired by classics like [i]Silent Hill[/i] and [i]Resident Evil 1, 2, and 3[/i].[/p][p]Hello, dear players:
[b]Tezcatlipoca[/b] was originally planned for release on [b]October 31st[/b] of this year. However, the game is already finished — and since I couldn't wait any longer, I’ve decided to [b]release it ahead of schedule[/b]![/p][p]This is [b]not a disguised early access[/b]: the game is fully complete and has been extensively tested. I’m not looking for free testers — but as with any human-made project, unexpected bugs may still appear. If you encounter a bug or crash, please report it in the official bug thread.[/p][p][b]Important note:[/b]
One character is currently missing some voice lines. These will be added in an upcoming update very soon.[/p][p][b]What’s next for Tezcatlipoca?[/b]
To keep both new and returning players engaged, the game will receive future updates. The next major feature will be [b]the option to play the entire game in first-person[/b], for a more immersive horror experience.
That’s right — you’ll soon be able to explore Tezcatlipoca [i]as if you were truly there[/i]...[/p][p]Thank you for playing, for supporting indie projects, and for facing the horrors that dwell beyond the mirror. 🖤[/p]

notes.title: Tezcatlipoca Demo is Out!
notes.content:
Thank you, lovely players—the demo is finally here! It features an ending and most of the town for you to explore.

While the final game will include additional areas and polished content, I’d love to hear from you. Share your experience playing, and of course, let me know about any bugs you encounter during your gameplay.

Get excited—the full release is coming on October 31, 2025!
